$comment: Declarative execution policy — the SINGLE source of truth for what an agent may run in this repo (étude 25 D-4). `npm run harness:sync` compiles it into per-tool views (today: .claude/settings.json); `npm run harness:check` fails CI if a view drifts from this file. Tools with no repo-level permission file (Codex, Cursor, …) read the human-readable summary in AGENTS.md § Execution policy instead — for them it is guidance, not enforcement; the hard net stays the husky hooks + required CI checks + the absence of prod credentials locally (étude 25 P-3/P-4).

allow.$comment: Always allowed — read-only inspection, the project's own gates, and (group `ops-dispatch`) the short list of workflows an agent may TRIGGER. That last group is the exception to `gh-readonly`, granted PER WORKFLOW and never as `gh workflow run:*`: the wildcard form would hand over db-migrate-prod.yml too. Most entries are reversible (rollback-prod's freeze/unfreeze) or read-only on prod (db-backup dumps, db-tests runs pgTAP on a throwaway database). The two `apply-content*` entries DO write prod, and are the deliberate exception (owner decision, 2026-07-28): a content campaign is prescribed end-to-end, and publishing was the one step it could not take. What makes them acceptable is that they publish nothing new — only the SQL compiled from a corpus that a merged PR and the Content CI gates already validated — idempotently, journalised in content_releases, with zero migration. `e2e-auth` joined them on 2026-08-22, and it is the one entry that MOVED out of `deny` — so here is the whole reasoning, because the next reader will find the old one in git. It was denied for a real incident: the run used to point the browser at a Vercel preview through PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL, that preview's SSR layer holds PROD Supabase secrets, and a spec filed a real `content_reports` row in production three nights running (#614; #638 is the same hole seen again, closed NOT_PLANNED once #618/#621 landed). Three things closed it, and this entry rests on all three: the workflow no longer sets PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL at all (Playwright spawns its own localhost dev server, fed with the TEST_SUPABASE_* secrets); its `workflow_dispatch` trigger declares NO inputs, so a dispatcher cannot redirect the run; and `findProdTarget` (scripts/shared/prod-targets.mjs) refuses from three independent places — playwright.config.ts, _env.mjs, reset-gameplay.mjs — if any URL resolves to the prod ref or a prod app host, so a mis-set TEST secret fails loudly instead of writing prod. What it DOES write is the dedicated TEST project (seed + gameplay reset), which is its purpose. Note the residual risk this entry accepts, identical to the one `apply-content` already accepts: `gh workflow run --ref <branch>` runs the workflow AS DEFINED ON THAT BRANCH, and the three guards live in files that branch could also edit — the net there is PR review, not this file. Re-deny the day the workflow gains a base-URL input or is pointed at a deployment again. What stays out writes prod OUTSIDE that reviewed path: the schema (db-migrate-prod) and a release/tag. Each is denied by name below so the reasoning survives the next reader. Adding a workflow here is a review decision, not a convenience. Grouped by intent so a reviewer sees WHY a rule exists, not just a flat list.

deny.reason: Prod migrates ONLY via db-migrate-prod.yml on merge (DoD §7) — a manual push strands prod behind code or applies unreviewed SQL.
Destructive: drops and recreates the database.
Same as the npx form — prod migrates only via db-migrate-prod.yml (DoD §7).
Same as the npx form — destructive.
Applies migrations to PROD. It runs on merge to `main` and nowhere else (DoD §7) — a manual dispatch would push schema that no PR gate ever saw.
Publishes a release/tag — outward-facing and hard to walk back. Tagging policy is a human call (docs/release-tagging-policy.md).
